newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures erase opening gains.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures erase opening gains.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures erased moderate opening gains, and most fell to moderate losses in early activity.

Floor brokers said after the market's runup Wednesday to all-time highs, its subsequent pullback and nearly flat close, players were waiting to see how the market adjusts and whether more long profittakers step in.

Small gains in U.S. Treasury bond futures, a rally in the dollar plus some good corporate earnings news added support at the outset Thursday, although a sizable drop in over-the-counter stocks bogged down values.

Some brokers had suspected that September Standard & Poor's (S&P) 500 futures might be reprising last week's price behavior, when futures surged to a peak on Wednesday and eroded for the balance of the week.
"I think they're going to start to bring it down," said one S&P 500 floor broker early Thursday before the market began selling off. "I think people will be covering (longs) today."
He also noted that futures open interest recently has risen in conjunction with prices, suggesting the contract has many open long positions that could be offset.

"So I just think it's more profittaking," said a floor analyst, who said some dealer selling triggered sellstops below 940.00 in September S&Ps. "The market is just a little overbought, but I don't think this is anything major."

He also noted some signs of arbitrage sell programs on the decline as the premium narrowed. Fair value was roughly 5.60 points premium. Arb buy programs need about 6.90 points over cash, and sell programs required about 5.10 points premium.

At 0919 CDT/1419 GMT, Sept S&Ps lost 3.55 pts to 937.70, Midcap lost 1.50 to 307.80, Russell off 1.85 to 409.75, Nikkei up 55.0 to 20,350.0, NASDAQ fell 14.00 to 1084.50. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
